speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; can you tell me when these symptoms first started and how high your fever reaches?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease.

The patient is an 11-year-old girl with a rash, low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. The description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area is highly specific for Kawasaki Disease, but the typical fever duration is usually at least 5 days and other classic signs like conjunctivitis or lymphadenopathy are missing. To confirm, I need to assess for other features.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology images of the rash and facial region.

Please describe any redness or swelling in your eyes, redness of your lips or tongue, or if your fingers or toes have become swollen or changed color.
